title: Timeline
subtitle: From a commercial dispute to an international wanted notice.
intro: The sequence of dates in this case matters more than any commentary. It shows: the man was not hiding, lived openly, worked and paid taxes — and only learned of his criminal prosecution at the moment of arrest in a foreign country.

events.title: External consultant — no complaints
events.text: Lagovsky works with JSC Fryazino Experimental Plant (JSC FEZ) as an external legal consultant under a services agreement. Not a staff employee, not authorised to make decisions — a retained lawyer. In over ten years of cooperation, no complaints were ever made about his work.

events.title: Corporate conflict
events.text: Minority shareholder S.V. Palkin initiates a series of pre-investigation inquiries and complaints — all without result. Context: attempts to gain control of the enterprise, which Lagovsky as a lawyer had lawfully resisted. In December 2021, the plant sells a land plot to another company — this transaction would later become the basis of the charges.

events.title: Criminal complaint filed
events.text: S.V. Palkin, through his lawyer V.O. Trofimchuk, files a complaint with law enforcement. Lagovsky's name is absent from the materials at this stage.

events.title: Criminal case opened
events.text: Investigator Yu.M. Salikov (Main Investigation Department, Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Russian Federation for the Moscow Region) opens case No. 12201460225000286 under Part 4, Article 159 of the Criminal Code. The case is opened without a complaint from the management of JSC FEZ — in violation of Part 3, Article 20 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Lagovsky is a witness. In December 2022 he is called in for questioning in that capacity — he is not detained and no charges are made.

events.title: Move to Serbia
events.text: Lagovsky's family legally relocates to Belgrade. Reasons: the war in Ukraine and the threat of forced mobilisation — Lagovsky holds a military rank and fears being conscripted to fight against Ukraine, where he was born and where his wife's relatives live. Residence permit obtained, official employment with tax payments. Departure was unimpeded — with a valid passport. Lagovsky knows nothing of any criminal case.

events.title: Secret charges filed
events.text: A year and a half after the case was opened, the investigation issues a resolution charging Lagovsky as an accused. The procedure takes place in absentia and in secret — without notifying Lagovsky himself, although his address in Serbia is known to the investigators. Until this moment he was a witness. In June 2024 Lagovsky independently checks his status on the Gosuslugi portal — the system shows he is not subject to criminal prosecution.

events.title: Arbitration: transaction found lawful
events.text: The Arbitration Court of the Moscow Region confirms: the transaction involving the sale of the land plot by JSC FEZ is entirely lawful, no damage occurred, and the price exceeds the cadastral value. The ruling is subsequently upheld through the entire chain of arbitration instances, including the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation. Criminal prosecution continues.

events.title: Arrest warrant in absentia and international wanted notice
events.text: 18 December — resolution on international wanted notice issued. 26 December — charges re-filed. 27 December — the Tversky District Court of Moscow issues an arrest warrant in absentia. The wanted notice is issued despite the known address of residence in Serbia — in violation of Article 210 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Lagovsky is still not notified of anything.

events.title: Arrest in Belgrade
events.text: Lagovsky is arrested at his home in Belgrade. He learns of the criminal case, the charges, and the international wanted notice for the first time — at the moment of arrest. 21 days in custody. Released on 29 April under a pledge not to leave the city of Belgrade; passport confiscated.

events.title: Serbian courts: formal review only
events.text: On 4 July the Higher Court of Belgrade approves extradition, finding that the request formally meets technical requirements. Defence evidence — including arbitration court rulings — was not examined: the court stated plainly that it was reviewing only the document from Moscow, not the substance of the charges. On 14 November the appeal upholds the ruling.

events.title: Asylum application
events.text: On 5 December Lagovsky expresses his intention to apply for asylum. On 10 December he submits a full application to the Asylum Office of the Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs. Grounds: real risk of forced mobilisation as a reservist, Ukrainian heritage, opposition to participation in the war against Ukraine.

events.title: Supreme Court of Serbia: request for protection of legality rejected
events.text: The Supreme Court (Kzz OK 1/2026) unanimously rejects the defence's request for protection of legality. Notably, the court declined to examine substantively the argument that Lagovsky was not a 'responsible person' — one of the key elements of the charges — characterising this as a question of fact rather than a violation of law. In doing so the court foreclosed the substance of the case behind a procedural formula.

events.title: Asylum denied
events.text: The Asylum Office of the Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs denies asylum and subsidiary protection (decision No. 26-7707/25). Reasoning: no grounds for persecution on Convention bases established; fear of mobilisation not classified as persecution. Lagovsky is ordered to leave Serbia within 15 days unless another basis for stay is found.

events.title: Asylum Commission: appeal rejected
events.text: The Asylum Commission (AŽ-23/26), chaired by Gordana Milanović, rejects the appeal against the Office's decision as unfounded, fully upholding the original refusal. No further appeal against the Commission's decision is permitted — the only remaining avenue is an administrative lawsuit before the Administrative Court of Serbia.

events.title: Administrative Court: last domestic instance
events.text: The case has been referred to the Administrative Court of Serbia. This is the last domestic instance on the asylum question. The court's ruling will determine whether Lagovsky is extradited to Russia or gains the right to remain in Serbia. International proceedings continue in parallel: UN, Interpol/CCF, ECHR.

summary: The timeline establishes three key facts. First: Lagovsky became an accused one and a half years after the case was opened — in secret, without notification, at a known address of residence, and only learned of it at the moment of arrest. Second: arbitration courts up to the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation found the same transaction lawful — the criminal prosecution was not halted. Third: not one Serbian court examined the defence evidence on the merits — each time the procedure was closed on formal grounds. The Administrative Court is the last domestic avenue.
